sections.html:
Windsor, the first English settlement in Connecticut, borders Hartford on the north and has a ZIP code of 06095. The town covers about 31.0 square miles, 29.5 of them land, and counted 29,492 residents in 2020. The Connecticut River marks its eastern edge, and the Farmington River joins it inside the town. Bloomfield, East Granby, Windsor Locks, South Windsor and East Windsor are the neighbors.

The ground is low. Day Hill, at 230 feet, is the high point, and the river itself, at 5 feet, is the low one. If your house is near the water, ask the town and FEMA about the parcel's flood zone, because buyers and their lenders will.

The town is a set of named communities rather than a single grid.

  • Windsor Center, with the train station and the Shad Derby Festival each spring.
  • Poquonock, which has its own elementary school.
  • Wilson, in the south near Hartford, named for a landowner who gave the railroad a right of way.
  • Hayden Station, in the north, named the same way.
  • Rainbow, a northern section; the Farmington River is dammed in the northwest corner to form the 234 acre Rainbow Reservoir.
  • Deerfield, the sixth principal community.

Use the village name when you describe a house.

Windsor has more ways in and out than most Connecticut suburbs. Interstates 91 and 291 cross town, Bradley International Airport borders it, and state routes 20, 75, 159, 178, 187, 218 and 305 add local links. Windsor station is served by the CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak, and CT Transit runs buses.

The station occupies the former Hartford and New Haven Railroad depot, and the Hartford Line double track was restored in 2018. For commuters that rail link is a selling point, since it offers an alternative to Interstate 91 traffic.

sections.h2: Why do some Windsor houses sell slowly?
sections.html:
Age, deferred maintenance and a spot near the river or an interstate are the usual reasons. Windsor grew from 10,068 people in 1940 to 19,467 in 1960 and 25,204 in 1980, so a large share of the housing was likely built in those decades, and the 2010 census counted 11,767 housing units.

Houses of that age may need a new roof or heating system, and a buyer with a mortgage can ask for that work before closing. An as-is cash sale removes the step. Compare the offer with a listing's net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs, not with the headline list price.

sections.h2: How a sale closes and what the state requires
sections.html:
Each Connecticut deed transfer triggers a state conveyance tax return, and the seller's side files it. The Department of Revenue Services requires Form OP-236 from the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an agent when the price is $2,000 or more, unless an exemption applies.

Form OP-236 pointWindsor answer
Who filesGrantor, grantor's attorney or authorized agent
WhenWhen the deed is recorded
Threshold$2,000 or more in consideration
Windsor town code164
Electronic optionmyCTREC, in participating towns

One exemption matters to stressed sellers. A principal residence sold for less than the mortgages plus priority real estate taxes and municipal liens can be exempt from the state tax. Ask your attorney whether it applies to your sale.

Ask the assessor and the tax collector for the current mill rate, any revaluation phase-in and the status of your tax bills. Unpaid property tax and municipal liens are paid from the sale proceeds, and a closing attorney orders a tax status check.

Connecticut law also lets a town add certain code enforcement expenses to the tax bill of a property that breaks health, safety or housing codes, so ask whether a charge like that sits on your parcel. Elderly or disability relief you qualify for should be applied to the bill. An owner who later gets proof of an exemption can request an abatement or refund, but only within one year of getting that proof.

Windsor's first English party arrived on September 26, 1633 and founded a trading post where the Farmington and Connecticut Rivers meet. The settlement took the name Windsor on February 21, 1637. For a seller the history matters in one respect. From 1957 to 2006 the town hosted the S1C Nuclear Powered Training Unit, a Navy prototype plant, and its site later became the first nuclear reactor site released for unrestricted use after demolition and decontamination.

A buyer who asks about industrial land near your street deserves a direct answer, and the town's planning office can supply it.

sections.h2: When repairs stand in the way
sections.html:
A new roof, a heating system or a foundation fix can stand between you and a listing. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so you skip the repairs, the showings and the wait on someone else's loan approval.

That convenience comes with a lower price than a repaired house might bring, so compare. Add up the repair estimates, the agent's commission and the months of carrying costs, then set the total against the cash offer. Send us the address and a short description of the condition, and we will give you a number to weigh.

sections.h2: Paying off what you owe at closing
sections.html:
A balance on the house does not prevent a sale. Mortgage payoffs, unpaid tax and liens are settled from the money at the table, and what remains goes to you. Your closing attorney requests each figure in writing, which is why it pays to know the amounts before you accept an offer.

Total them on one page. If the sum comes close to the price, you want to hear that now, not at the signing. Talk through options such as the state's exemption for a principal residence sold for too little to cover its debts, and let the attorney say whether it applies.

1. You and the buyer meet with the attorney, or sign separately if that is easier.
  2. You sign the deed and the conveyance tax return.
  3. The attorney pays the lender, the tax office and any lien holder from the proceeds.
  4. The deed is recorded at the town clerk's office, and the sale is complete.
  5. You hand over keys, garage openers and any manuals or warranties.

Bring identification and the paperwork the attorney asked for, and cancel your own utilities and insurance afterward.

• Find your deed and the latest tax bill.
  • Write down what you owe on a mortgage or lien.
  • Note which village the house is in.
  • List the repairs you know are needed.
  • Decide who can sign if the house belongs to an estate.

A buyer can answer faster when these are in front of you, and you will not be pushed into agreeing to a figure before you have the facts. Write the names and phone numbers of everyone involved on the same page.

faqs.a: Windsor covers about 31.0 square miles, with 29.5 square miles of land, and had 29,492 residents in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: Is there train service in Windsor?
faqs.a: Yes. Windsor station is served by the CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak's Northeast Regional and Valley Eagle trains.
The principal communities are Deerfield, Hayden Station, Poquonock, Rainbow, Wilson and Windsor Center.

faqs.q: What is the Windsor code on the state conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The state lists 164 as Windsor's town code on Form OP-236. The seller's side files the return when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Windsor house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A mortgage-financed buyer may demand repairs, while a cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands.
